verdicts.justification: load('sotus') returned "type: <class 'sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline'>" and repr raised "AttributeError : 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'transform_input'". Source confirms the root cause: hypertools/io/load.py line 24 'sotus': '1J0MBhpRwdT2WChfWJ4HXYq6jU4XpyJPm' is identical to line 27 'nips_model': '1J0MBhpRwdT2WChfWJ4HXYq6jU4XpyJPm', and cached files hash identically (sotus == nips_model == 4f93308a48002730866659bda7ef393f5451dc8360b9e3c91c9cf5d77f73a762) while sotus_model and nips differ. Docstring (load.py:167) promises 'a collection of State of the Union speeches from 1989-2018'. Documented dataset returns entirely wrong (and broken) object: critical is fair.
commands_run: env PYTHONPATH=/Users/jmanning/hypertools MPLBACKEND=Agg .venv/bin/python -c "import hypertools as hyp; d=hyp.load('sotus'); print(type(d)); print(repr(d))"

verdicts.justification: Loading wiki_model emitted three sklearn/base.py:463 InconsistentVersionWarning messages ('Trying to unpickle estimator CountVectorizer from version 1.0.2 when using version 1.8.0', likewise LatentDirichletAllocation and Pipeline). m.transform(['the quick brown fox']).shape == (1, 50) works, but repr(m) raises "AttributeError : 'Pipeline' object has no attribute 'transform_input'" — so merely displaying the returned model in a REPL/notebook crashes.
